paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: when the world looks unjust, you can take it straight to the LORD. This writer doesn't hide his anger or his "How long" question (Psalm 94:3). He says it right to God and asks Him to "Rise up, O Judge of the earth" (Psalm 94:2). You don't have to pretend everything is fine, and you don't have to fix it yourself.

The wicked say "The LORD does not see," but the writer answers with a question that settles it: "He who formed the eye, can He not see?" (Psalm 94:7, 9). God sees, God hears, and God knows every thought. Then the writer calls blessed the man the LORD disciplines and teaches from His law, because it gives him relief from days of trouble (Psalm 94:12-13). So when things feel out of control, God's Word is where He steadies you. And here's the promise underneath it all: "the LORD will not forsake His people" (Psalm 94:14).

The writer isn't just talking big, either. He's been there, and he says when his foot was slipping, "Your loving devotion, O LORD, supports me" (Psalm 94:18). When anxiety overwhelmed him, he says "Your consolation delights my soul" (Psalm 94:19). In the end he says "the LORD has been my stronghold, and my God is my rock of refuge" (Psalm 94:22). So bring the unfair stuff and the anxious stuff to Him, baker, because He is the safe place the writer ran to.
